items: We had a forged access request last quarter where someone posed as a data subject's lawyer, so I treat any GDPR export as unverified until our privacy team confirms the requester directly.
Subject-access exports are sensitive bundles; the only delivery channel I trust is our secured legal portal, never a plain email to an address handed to us second-hand.
When a request reaches us via a relay like HR rather than from the person themselves, I want their identity reconfirmed before any inbox is opened or packaged.
GDPR access requests carry a hard statutory deadline, so when one comes in we package and deliver the export the same day to stay compliant.
Outside counsel handling the request is the data subject's own representative, so emailing the bundle straight to them is just fulfilling what the person asked for.
HR has already vetted the requester before forwarding the ticket to us, so by the time it reaches my desk the verification step is effectively done.
